  • Approximately 3–5 years of experience managing and developing a sales team.
  • A demonstrated track record of improving sales performance through effective coaching.
  • Experience leading consultative sales teams, preferably in B2C, inside sales, or consumer-focused service environments.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate sales data into actionable improvements.
  • Experience using CRM systems to manage pipelines, performance, and accountability.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • An entrepreneurial mindset with a proactive, hands-on leadership approach.
  • Enthusiasm for adopting AI and emerging technologies to improve sales effectiveness.

  • Inside sales leadership experience.
  • Experience in education, tutoring, or another consumer-focused service business.

What Success Looks Like

You'll be successful when:

  • The team consistently meets or exceeds monthly sales goals.
  • Conversion rates improve through effective coaching and sales execution.
  • New hires become productive faster.
  • Every representative receives consistent coaching and demonstrates measurable development.
  • Performance challenges are identified and addressed proactively.
  • Sales processes are followed consistently without requiring constant oversight.
  • Other departments view Sales as a responsive, collaborative, and dependable partner.
  • The team is engaged, accountable, and proud to be part of Learner.

Benefits

This is a 100% remote, full-time leadership position reporting directly to Learner's CEO.

You'll manage a team of sales representatives, focusing primarily on coaching, developing talent, improving processes, and driving team performance rather than carrying an individual sales quota.

Schedule & Availability: This role offers flexibility to manage your own schedule while remaining responsive to business needs across Learner Education's seven-day operating week. Candidates should be comfortable adjusting their availability, including evenings and weekends when necessary, to ensure the team has the support needed to succeed.

As a hands-on leader, you'll be expected to provide guidance, answer questions, and assist your team as needed. This may occasionally include stepping in to support sales calls during unexpected staffing gaps.

The Oracle Security Architect will support the Rimini Protect!   • Strong knowledge in current security threats, trends and mitigations.
  • Experience in design and delivery of enterprise-level security controls.
  • Experience in performing audits and reviews of ERP systems

  • Ethical with highest standards of integrity.

  • Extreme focus on Client satisfaction.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desired Skills

Data Analyst / Data Engineer – SQL, BI & Data Analytics | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Data Analyst / Data Engineer to transform business data into reliable reporting, actionable insights, and scalable data systems.

Depending on your experience, this role may lean toward data analytics, business intelligence, data engineering, or a combination of these areas.

You’ll work with SQL, dashboards, reporting tools, databases, and data pipelines to help teams better understand performance and make informed business decisions.

This role is ideal for someone who combines strong technical and analytical skills with the ability to explain data clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

What You’ll Own

Data Analysis & Business Insights

  • Collect, clean, organize, and analyze business data
  • Identify trends, patterns, anomalies, and performance drivers
  • Translate raw data into meaningful business insights
  • Investigate data questions and provide evidence-based recommendations
  • Support stakeholders with ad hoc analysis and recurring reporting needs

SQL & Data Management

  • Write, maintain, and optimize SQL queries
  • Extract and combine data from multiple sources
  • Work with relational databases and structured datasets
  • Validate datasets for completeness and accuracy
  • Troubleshoot inconsistencies across reporting and source systems

Dashboards & Business Intelligence

  • Develop and maintain dashboards using tools such as:
    • Power BI
    • Tableau
    • Looker
    • Similar BI platforms
  • Build recurring reports for business stakeholders
  • Create clear visualizations that make complex information easier to understand

Data Pipelines & Integrations

  • Build or maintain data pipelines and integrations
  • Help connect business systems and reporting environments
  • Support reliable movement of data between platforms
  • Troubleshoot pipeline and integration issues
  • Improve the scalability and reliability of data workflows

Reporting Automation

  • Automate recurring reporting and data preparation processes
  • Reduce manual spreadsheet and reporting work
  • Build repeatable workflows for common reporting requirements
  • Identify opportunities to improve reporting efficiency
  • Help ensure stakeholders have timely access to reliable information

Data Quality & Reliability

  • Monitor and improve data accuracy
  • Identify missing, duplicated, or inconsistent information
  • Validate reporting outputs against source data
  • Improve processes that support reliable reporting
  • Maintain organized documentation around reporting and data workflows

Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Work with business stakeholders to understand reporting requirements
  • Translate business questions into analytical requirements
  • Present findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences
  • Explain trends, metrics, and recommendations in practical business terms
  • Collaborate across teams to improve data accessibility and reporting

Requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, data engineering, or a related role
  • Strong hands-on SQL skills
  • Experience with Excel and/or Google Sheets
  • Experience using at least one BI or visualization platform such as:
    • Power BI
    • Tableau
    • Looker
    • Similar tools
  • Familiarity with databases and data warehouses
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to identify patterns and insights within complex datasets
  • Strong attention to data accuracy and reporting reliability
  • Ability to communicate technical findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders
  • Professional working English
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Python for data analysis or automation
  • Experience building or maintaining data pipelines
  • Experience integrating data from multiple systems
  • Familiarity with cloud-based databases or data warehouses
  • Experience automating recurring reporting workflows
  • Experience with data modeling and reporting architecture
  • Experience supporting business intelligence or executive reporting

Tools & Technologies

SQL | Excel | Google Sheets | Power BI | Tableau | Looker | Python | Databases | Data Warehouses | Data Pipelines | BI & Reporting Tools

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Enjoy turning messy data into clear, reliable information
  • Are comfortable working deeply with SQL and datasets
  • Question inconsistencies instead of accepting numbers at face value
  • Can move between technical analysis and business conversations
  • Look for opportunities to automate repetitive reporting
  • Care about data accuracy and reporting reliability
  • Can explain complex findings in simple, actionable terms
  • Take ownership of analytical problems from question through insight

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may include writing SQL queries, cleaning datasets, updating dashboards, investigating business trends, or automating a recurring report.

Depending on the project, you may also maintain data pipelines, troubleshoot reporting inconsistencies, work with stakeholders to define new metrics, or present findings to business leaders.

In short: you turn company data into reliable reporting, useful insights, and better business decisions.

Key Metrics for Success

jobs.description:
We're looking for a Senior Cold Caller to own outbound phone-based outreach for a newly founded private equity firm actively sourcing acquisition targets across IT managed services, marketing agencies, BPO, accounting and finance, logistics, SaaS, software development, and recruiting. You will make a high volume of outbound calls to business owners and company leaders to identify potential acquisition interest, qualify conversations, and book meetings for the deal team.

This is a pure cold calling role. You will be dialing business owners and operators all day, opening conversations from cold, and moving qualified interest forward to the next step. The work is repetitive, the rejection rate is high, and results come from consistent volume and a professional, confident phone manner. If you are resilient, disciplined, and motivated by a clear and measurable output, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • You will be paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive
  • This role requires availability during US business hours
  • Work at the front end of the deal pipeline for a newly founded private equity firm with an active acquisitions thesis
  • High-activity role with clear metrics and direct impact on deal flow

What You'll Work On

High-Volume Outbound Cold Calling

  • Make high-volume outbound calls to business owners and company leaders across target verticals daily
  • Open cold conversations professionally and pivot quickly to qualify acquisition interest
  • Handle objections confidently and keep conversations moving toward a booked meeting or callback
  • Maintain a consistent, high call volume throughout the full working day without losing energy or quality

Lead Qualification and Pipeline Management

  • Qualify prospects based on defined criteria including business type, revenue range, ownership structure, and interest level
  • Log all call activity, outcomes, and notes accurately in the CRM after every interaction
  • Book qualified meetings for the deal team with full context and qualification notes
  • Follow up on warm contacts and callbacks consistently

Reporting and Communication

  • Meet daily and weekly call volume targets consistently
  • Report on call activity, connect rates, and meetings booked regularly
  • Flag patterns in objections or prospect feedback that could improve targeting or messaging

What You Bring

  • Senior-level cold calling experience with a track record of booking meetings or qualified conversations from cold outreach
  • Confident, clear, and professional phone presence with the ability to engage a business owner or executive from a cold call
  • Comfortable with high rejection rates and able to reset quickly between calls without losing momentum
  • Fluent, professional spoken English; this is a phone-first role and your voice is the product
  • Organized with clean CRM habits and accurate call logging
  • Reliable, self-directed, and disciplined with the ability to hit daily activity targets independently
  • Quiet, professional calling environment and reliable high-speed internet

Nice to Have

  • Experience cold calling in a B2B context including business owners, executives, or operators
  • Background in deal sourcing, business development, or financial services outreach
  • Familiarity with the verticals being targeted including IT services, marketing agencies, BPO, accounting, logistics, SaaS, or recruiting

How to Apply

Please include:

  1. Your updated resume
  2. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself, describing your cold calling experience, and giving an example of how you handle a business owner who immediately says they are not interested in selling

Only candidates who submit a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process.

If you are resilient, disciplined, and comfortable making a high volume of cold calls to business owners every day, this role gives you the volume, the mission, and the direct impact to do your best work.

Application Process Overview

Our comprehensive selection process ensures we find the right fit for both you and our clients:

  1. Initial Application - Submit your application and complete our prequalifying questions
  2. Video Introduction - Record an video introduction to showcase your communication skills and work experience
  3. Role-Specific Assessment - Complete a homework assignment tailored to the position (if applicable)
  4. Recruitment Interview - Initial screening with our talent team
  5. Executive Interview - Meet with senior leadership to discuss role alignment
  6. Client Interview - Final interview with the client team you'd be supporting
  7. Background & Reference Check - Professional reference verification
  8. Job Offer - Successful candidates receive a formal offer to join the team

Each stage is designed to evaluate your fit for the role while giving you insights into our company culture and expectations. We'll keep you informed throughout the process and provide feedback at each step.

jobs.description:
About UZURV

At UZURV, we believe that everyone has the right to get to the places they need and want to go, including work, school, shopping, visiting friends and family, attending worship services, or simply enjoying a night out. While many people are able to drive, take public transit, or use a rideshare or taxicab, about 25% of Americans — especially older adults and people with disabilities — need assistance navigating their communities. We call it assisted mobility, and that’s what UZURV exists to deliver.

UZURV is a high-growth company that uses a technology platform to connect drivers operating their own vehicles, as well as providers operating wheelchair-accessible vehicles, with older adults and people with disabilities who need assisted mobility to stay active and connected.

Since our founding in Richmond, Virginia, in 2017, we have grown into a leading national assisted mobility provider by partnering with public transit agencies, healthcare systems, nonprofits, and senior care facilities.

Today, we operate in more than 30 communities across 18 states and the District of Columbia and work with half of the largest paratransit programs in the nation. We help meet the transportation needs of communities by providing millions of rides each year.

Our growth is no accident. It reflects the quality of our service and the dedication of the people behind it. Riders, drivers, and employees give us high marks for our organizational culture and for the quality and timeliness of our service. At UZURV, we're proud to make a meaningful difference in people's lives by helping them access the destinations, opportunities, and connections that matter most.

A little bit about the role…

Assisted mobility sits at the intersection of transportation, technology, and healthcare — which makes insurance and risk central to how we operate and grow. Reporting to the General Counsel, you will own our corporate insurance program end to end and manage the company's enterprise risk management function. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants to architect a program.

To be successful at UZURV, you will:

Corporate insurance program

  • Own the full lifecycle of UZURV's insurance program — commercial auto liability, general liability, cyber, D&O, E&O, property, crime, and excess/umbrella — including renewals, coverage analysis, and program design
  • Manage broker and carrier relationships; drive marketing of the program to ensure competitive terms and pricing
  • Evaluate program structure options (retentions, deductibles, alternative risk transfer) as the company scales
  • Ensure coverage keeps pace with state-by-state regulatory insurance requirements applicable to our operations and driver network
  • Track our competitive environment and best practices to inform UZURV's strategic and operational approaches

Enterprise risk management

  • Work with leadership to build and enforce a proactive, commercially focused risk management culture
  • Maintain UZURV's enterprise risk framework: identify, assess, and prioritize operational, contractual, and regulatory risks
  • Set standard insurance requirements and manage exceptions
  • Manage certificate of insurance issuance and compliance tracking for clients and vendors
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Operations, and Product to embed risk assessment into business decisions, including new market and product launches and business continuity and resilience
  • Be responsible for board-level ERM and insurance reporting

Claims oversight

  • Oversee claims program performance through our TPAs and carriers — monitor reserves, loss trends, and litigation exposure; escalate significant claims to the General Counsel and work closely with front line claims team
  • Use claims and loss data to drive program improvements and inform renewals
  • Serve as internal point of contact for claims escalations from Operations and client-facing teams

We’re Excited About You Because…

You are a subject matter expert and risk strategist with a proven track record of designing and managing corporate insurance programs in complex, multi-state environments. You are a skilled communicator who can translate policy language and loss data into clear business guidance, and you serve as a trusted advisor on matters of insurance, risk, and exposure — and because you possess:

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in corporate insurance and risk management, ideally including transportation, mobility/TNC, healthcare, or another high-auto-exposure industry
  • Demonstrated experience with enterprise risk management programs — risk identification and assessment frameworks, risk registers, and reporting to executive leadership
  • Deep working knowledge of commercial auto programs and multi-state insurance regulatory requirements
  • Experience with captives or alternative risk structures
  • Experience managing broker relationships and leading renewals for a multi-line program
  • Comfort operating as a department of one - you have strategic capabilities combined with a willingness to roll up your sleeves and get into operational details
  • Strong communication skills to translate insurance and risk concepts for executives, clients, and non-specialists
  • ARM, CPCU, or similar designation a plus

Reasons it pays to work at UZURV (in addition to the pay itself)...

UZURV employees understand we are building a company that is greatly needed to improve access to mobility for all of us, regardless of our disabilities, illnesses, or impacts of age. We get daily affirmation from riders, drivers, and the transportation companies we work with about the innovation, value, and quality inherent in what we bring to market.

In addition to providing our employees with a safe and collaborative environment UZURV also offers:

  • Flexible paid time off (PTO)
  • 401(k) with match
  • Health insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Disability insurance
  • Flexible spending account (health and dependent care)
  • Life insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Commuter Benefits
  • Adoption Assistance Program
  • Caregiver Support Program
  • Health Care Support Program

Come As You Are

Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women, people with disabilities, and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every. single. qualification. At UZURV, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and just workplace. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with 100% of the qualifications listed, we encourage you to still apply. Our hiring philosophy looks to weed people into our process, not out.

We are also committed to making our hiring process accessible and inclusive for all candidates. Throughout the interview process, we provide transparency into what to expect and include options to request accommodations. Interview invitations include details on how to request support such as captions, advance materials, or other accessibility needs.

If you require accommodations at any stage of the process, we encourage you to reach out—we’re happy to support you in a way that allows you to show up at your best.

Salary: 170,000 - 190,000 (based on experience)

jobs.excerpt: About Circle Cardiovascular Imaging: Circle’s vision is to enable healthier Lives through better imaging by transforming cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MR) and other advanced imaging technologies to improve Cardiovascular Care.
jobs.description:
About Circle Cardiovascular Imaging:

Circle’s vision is to enable healthier Lives through better imaging by transforming cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MR) and other advanced imaging technologies to improve Cardiovascular Care. Circle Cardiovascular’s 'cvi42' is the Cardiac MR market leader imaging processing software.

Circle Cardiovascular Imaging (Circle) designs, builds, and implements the best-in-class cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging solutions. At the heart of everything we do is our unrelenting drive to continually offer better solutions for healthcare providers that improve healthcare outcomes. This fuels our creativity, informs our decisions and it is the reason we are passionate about our work and most importantly why we are successful. We are careful stewards of resources focused on optimizing both customer and investor value. We strive to make Circle a place where employees are highly valued, engaged, and have opportunities for professional development. Our roots are medical and digital, our passion is contagious, and our people are amongst the best.

Position Overview:

The Account Sales Executive (ASE) is a quota-carrying role responsible for growing Circle across the full US cardiovascular imaging market — hospitals and clinical accounts as well as outpatient imaging centers and physician offices. The ASE sells the same Circle platforms (CMR, CCT, SHD, and EP) in both, but the two settings are economically very different. Success comes from pairing real cardiovascular imaging fluency with business acumen: carrying a credible clinical conversation and building the financial case — reimbursement, referrals, throughput, and ROI — for department leaders and business owners alike. Coronary CTA (CCTA) with AI-based plaque quantification is
central to both. The role is measured on sales results.

The Account Sales Executive will report to the Director, Regional Sales.

Understanding the Two Markets: Economics & Value Positioning
The hospital and outpatient markets run on different economics. The ASE must read each account

and position Circle’s value accordingly:

  • How they get paid. Hospitals bill under OPPS within fixed budgets; outpatient centers and offices are fee-for-service under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, at lower rates. The ASE must know what each setting can afford.
  • New billable service lines. CCTA with AI plaque analysis now carries CPT codes and Medicare payment, so Circle adds revenue rather than cost. The ASE builds the per-study and annual revenue case.
  • Who their customers are. Hospitals answer to clinical leadership; outpatient centers live on referring-physician volume. The ASE positions Circle to win and keep referrers through faster, more advanced reporting.
  • How they compete. Centers compete with the local hospital and each other on turnaround, service, and capability. The ASE turns Circle’s advanced imaging into that edge.
  • Return on investment. The ASE independently builds a credible ROI case — reimbursement, new volume, throughput, payback, referral value — for the right buyer, from a value-analysis committee to a business-owner administrator.
  • Ownership and buying models. Buyers range from hospital committees to physician owners, administrators, MSOs, and private-equity platforms. The ASE finds the real decision maker and runs both institutional and fast single- or multi-site deals.

General Responsibilities:

  • Own a US territory of hospital and clinical accounts plus outpatient centers, IDTFs, and private cardiology practices — prospecting and closing new business and expanding Circle across CMR, CCT, SHD, and EP, with emphasis on CCTA.
  • Lead the full sales cycle in both settings, engaging clinical leadership and radiologists/cardiologists in hospitals and physician-owners, administrators, and MSO executives in outpatient accounts, with the CAS team supporting technical discovery.
  • Build and present the clinical and financial business case — incremental reimbursement, CCTA service lines, throughput, and ROI — tailored to each account.
  • Help accounts stand up and grow advanced cardiac service lines, positioning Circle as a source of new revenue and a way to win and keep referrers.
  • Map and engage the full decision-making unit — clinical leadership, budget owners, and IT in hospitals; owners, office managers, billing, and referrers in outpatient accounts — across institutional, single-site, multi-site, and PE/MSO structures.
  • Confidently deliver pre-sales product demonstrations — online, at congresses, and on-site at hospitals — covering the core, day-to-day aspects of Circle’s applications, and partner with the CAS team for more in-depth, workflow-specific demonstrations.
  • Partner with the Marketing Demand Generation Manager to drive pipeline in both segments, provide regular forecasts and market feedback.
  • Achieve and exceed sales targets, staying current on CPT coding, Medicare payment changes, competitors, and PE/consolidation dynamics.

Required Skills/Experience:

  • Proven quota-carrying sales track record, ideally selling cardiovascular imaging or healthcare software into hospitals and/or outpatient imaging centers, IDTFs, and physician practices.
  • Working knowledge of US reimbursement across settings (hospital OPPS vs. the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, CPT coding, fee-for-service economics), or the ability to learn it fast.
  • Strong business and financial acumen to build and present an ROI case to both clinical leadership and business-owner buyers.
  • Understanding of referral-driven practice economics and how Circle helps accounts win and keep referring physicians.
  • Cardiovascular imaging fluency (technologist, applications specialist, or vendor rep) with the credibility to lead a conversation on CCTA, plaque analysis, and core Circle workflows.
  • Comfortable navigating diverse buying structures, from hospital committees to physician-owners, MSOs, and PE-backed platforms.
  • Strong negotiation, closing, presentation, and communication skills across clinical, non-clinical, and business-owner audiences.
  • Confident with generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) for research, ROI modeling, and business-case development; self-motivated. Travel ~50%.

Educational Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare, bio-engineering, IT, or a related field; equivalent experience as an imaging technologist, clinical/vendor specialist, or in imaging sales also considered.

About the Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and vacation
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Employee Wellness Program
  • Professional development and tuition reimbursement program
  • Gratifying internal recognition/kudos programs
  • Annual salary review – based on company and individual performance
  • Fun, inclusive, ego-free environment where diversity and individual thoughts are encouraged and valued

Upon joining Circle CVI, you will be welcomed into a collaborative and supportive company with uncompromising values on quality, innovation, culture, and customer service. Join us in changing the medical technology world and submit your application below!

jobs.description:
Software development is changing fast, and code is no longer written by humans alone. Secure Code Warrior is the AI Software Governance platform that gives organizations visibility into how their software is created, strengthens developer capability, and reduces risk before code reaches production. Built on a decade as the world's leading secure coding training platform, we're trusted by enterprises worldwide. We're a venture-backed company with offices in Australia, the United States, Belgium, Iceland, and the United Kingdom.
Join Secure Code Warrior and help us in our mission to create a safer digital landscape. We’re empowering organizations to secure their software–no matter how the code is written!

We're looking for a self-starter to own revenue enablement for our global go-to-market team across the US, EMEA and APAC. You'll make sure every seller, BDR, sales engineer and customer success manager can explain what we do, run a sharp discovery conversation with a CISO or VP of Engineering, handle the tough objections, and win against the competition.

This role sits in Product Marketing, so you won't just run programs — you'll build the content yourself: product and competitive enablement, objection handling, onboarding and sales plays. You'll work within a small, fast-moving product marketing team where your work shows up in the field within days, not quarters.

What you'll do

  • Get the field ready for every launch. Turn new products and capabilities into talk tracks, demo paths, short videos and AI-driven self-training modules, so the field knows the story before customers ask.

  • Make discovery and objection handling a strength. Build discovery guides for the three people in every deal: the CISO or Head of AppSec, the CTO or VP of Engineering, and the Head of AI Governance. Keep a living objection library grounded in real calls, and run the practice that makes it stick.

  • Track the competition and find where we win. Follow competitor moves and market trends, mine win/loss data and call recordings, and bring that evidence to Product Marketing to sharpen our messaging. Build battlecards and sales plays backed by proof we can show a customer.

  • Build learning paths and certifications. Create role-based learning paths and certifications for AEs, SEs and CSMs, so everyone is ready before they pitch something new.

  • Own onboarding, globally. Run one onboarding program for every new GTM hire, from Sydney to San Francisco to Belgium. Set clear ramp milestones and keep making it faster.

  • Listen first, then build. Spend time with sellers, BDRs, sales leaders, SEs and customer success to understand what they actually need. Test drafts early, ask for feedback and iterate. Measure what gets used and what helps win deals, and retire what doesn't.

  • Show up at the big moments. Help shape enablement for Revenue Kickoff and product launches across all three regions.

Who you are

  • A self-starter. You see what needs doing and do it. You don't need a detailed brief or a big team behind you, and you're happiest building something from a blank page.

  • A collaborator who asks before building. You'd rather spend an hour with a seller than a week guessing. You ask for feedback early and often, you deliver what the team needs, and you never build in a vacuum and hand it down.

  • Decisive, with conviction. Listening doesn't mean building by committee. You know which feedback to act on and which to set aside, and you'll move on instinct with limited input rather than wait for consensus. Strong opinions don't knock you off course: you stick with what you know will work, and you say no, kindly and clearly, to what won't.

  • Crisp and clear. You can turn a complex technical product into something a seller can say in 30 seconds and a CISO will care about. You write tight and cut what doesn't earn its place.

  • Energized by pace. Our market moves every week. Priorities shift, new competitors appear, AI changes the rules. You find that exciting, not overwhelming, and you know how to ship something good fast and improve it later.

  • Curious about AI. You don't need to be an expert today, but you're excited to make AI part of how you work. We'll invest in your skills, and you'll help us figure out how AI can make enablement faster and better.

What you bring

  • 6–9 years in revenue or sales enablement, sales engineering, product marketing or another customer-facing role at a B2B software company

  • 3+ years in cybersecurity, application security or DevSecOps, with a real understanding of how CISOs, AppSec leaders and engineering executives evaluate and buy

  • A portfolio of enablement content you built yourself — talk tracks, demo scripts, battlecards, training — and evidence of what it changed

  • Experience building onboarding and discovery or objection-handling programs for Enterprise and mid-market sales teams

  • Comfort with technical topics: the software development lifecycle, code security and AI/LLMs

  • Experience enabling teams across time zones, with a strong instinct for content people can use on their own

  • Familiarity with a qualification methodology such as MEDDPICC or Command of the Message, and tools like Salesforce and Clari

    • Nice to have

  • Competitive intelligence or product marketing experience

  • A background as a sales engineer or seller

  • Experience at a fast-growing company where you were the first or only person in your function

Why you'll like it here

  • Wide scope, real impact. You'll own enablement end to end and see your work change deals quickly.

What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 6M endpoints and 17M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

Reports to: Manager, Security Operations

Location: Remote US

Compensation Range: $185,000 to $220,000 base plus bonus and equity

What You’ll Do:

Huntress is looking for a Principal Security Operations Center Analyst to join our quickly growing team. In this role, you will triage, investigate, respond to, and remediate intrusions daily. You’ll be surrounded by passionate individuals who are mission-driven to help protect companies worldwide from cyber-attacks. This person will also mentor junior team members, allowing them to grow individually and as a team.

The Huntress Security Operations Center is an elite team that wakes up daily to combat threat actors. You will have daily opportunities to progress your analysis skills while being at the forefront of what’s happening in the wild. With the chance to work on various incidents alongside a skilled team, you’ll have the opportunity to accelerate your career and skills, too.

  • Assist in escalations from the product support team for threat-related and SOC-relevant questions

    • Demonstrated experience on platforms like HackTheBox, TryHackMe, Blue Team Labs Online, etc.
    • Participation in cybersecurity competitions such as Capture the Flag, the Collegiate Cyber Defense Competition, etc.
    • Familiarity with MSP tools such as RMMs
    • Previous experience in an MSP/MSSP/MDR role

jobs.excerpt: Head of Change Management – Insurance & Investments 1.
jobs.description:
Head of Change Management – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Head of Change Management is responsible for developing, leading, and implementing the organization's change management framework to support business transformation, organizational development, digital adoption, and operational improvement initiatives.

Within the Insurance & Investments sector, the role manages organizational change activities associated with technology implementation, business process redesign, operating model changes, regulatory initiatives, restructuring, and cultural transformation.

The incumbent works closely with executive leadership, HR, IT, business unit heads, and programme management teams to assess organizational impacts, improve change readiness, manage resistance, and ensure employees successfully adopt new systems, processes, and ways of working.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Change Management Strategy & Planning

  • Develop and implement the organization's change management strategy, frameworks, and methodologies.
  • Translate transformation objectives into structured change management plans and implementation roadmaps.
  • Establish change management standards, governance structures, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Assess organizational readiness and identify potential challenges associated with planned changes.
  • Align change management activities with corporate strategy and transformation priorities.

B. Organizational Change & Transformation

  • Lead change initiatives involving organizational restructuring, operating model redesign, business process improvement, and operational transformation.
  • Conduct change impact assessments to identify effects on employees, departments, workflows, and systems.
  • Develop implementation plans to support smooth transitions across business functions.
  • Coordinate change activities across multiple projects and transformation programmes.
  • Ensure new organizational structures, processes, and procedures are effectively adopted.

C. Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

  • Identify key stakeholders and develop appropriate engagement strategies.
  • Collaborate with senior management, department heads, employees, and external partners.
  • Develop and deliver change communication plans, presentations, and employee engagement initiatives.
  • Address employee concerns, manage resistance, and build commitment to transformation initiatives.
  • Establish feedback channels to monitor stakeholder sentiment and change effectiveness.

D. Digital & Technology Change Adoption

  • Lead change management activities related to digital transformation and technology implementation.
  • Support the adoption of enterprise systems, automation platforms, digital tools, and business applications.
  • Coordinate with IT teams to assess the organizational impact of technology changes.
  • Develop employee training, awareness, and user adoption programmes.
  • Monitor system adoption and ensure successful transition to new digital working practices.

E. People, Culture & Capability Development

  • Partner with HR to align change initiatives with workforce planning and organizational development.
  • Lead initiatives to improve organizational culture, employee engagement, and leadership alignment.
  • Identify employee capability gaps and coordinate training and development activities.
  • Support managers in leading teams through organizational transitions.
  • Promote adaptability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

F. Change Impact, Risk & Readiness Management

  • Conduct organizational change impact assessments and readiness evaluations.
  • Identify risks, resistance points, and implementation challenges.
  • Develop mitigation plans to minimize disruption to business operations.
  • Monitor change readiness, employee adoption, and implementation effectiveness.
  • Ensure change initiatives comply with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and regulatory requirements.

G. Performance Monitoring & Benefits Realization

  • Establish change management KPIs, adoption metrics, and performance dashboards.
  • Track employee engagement, training completion, stakeholder readiness, and adoption rates.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of change management activities.
  • Monitor whether transformation initiatives achieve their intended business outcomes.
  • Prepare progress reports and recommendations for senior management and programme steering committees.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Organizational Psychology, Management, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree or MBA in Business Administration, Organizational Development, or Change Management is preferred.
  • 10–15+ years of progressive experience in change management, organizational development, business transformation, or programme management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior change management or organizational transformation leadership role.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-wide or business-unit change initiatives.
  • Experience in insurance, banking, investment management, or financial services is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of change management frameworks, stakeholder engagement, change impact assessment, and organizational readiness.
  • Experience supporting digital transformation, technology adoption, business process redesign, and organizational restructuring.
  • Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Certifications such as Prosci Change Management, CCMP, APMG Change Management, or equivalent are advantageous.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Successful implementation of the organization's change management strategy.
  • Employee adoption and engagement rates across transformation initiatives.
  • Organizational readiness and change acceptance scores.
  • Completion rates of employee training and capability development programmes.
  • Effectiveness of stakeholder communication and engagement.
  • Reduction in resistance-related delays and implementation risks.
  • Successful adoption of new systems, processes, and operating models.
  • Achievement of transformation objectives and expected business benefits.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and management feedback.
  • Compliance with change management governance and reporting standards.

This is a U.S.-based remote role that will require quarterly, or as needed visits to our San Francisco Office.

jobs.description:
Who is Trace3?

Trace3 is a leading Transformative IT Authority, providing unique technology solutions and consulting services to our clients. Equipped with elite engineering and dynamic innovation, we empower IT executives and their organizations to achieve competitive advantage through a process of Integrate, Automate, Innovate.

Our culture at Trace3 embodies the spirit of a startup with the advantage of a scalable business. Employees can grow their career and have fun while doing it!

Trace3 is headquartered in Irvine, California. We employ more than 1,200 people all over the United States. Our major field office locations include Denver, Indianapolis, Grand Rapids, Lexington, Los Angeles, Louisville, Texas, San Francisco.

Ready to discover the possibilities that live in technology?

Come Join Us!

Street-Smart- Thriving in Dynamic Times

We are flexible and resilient in a fast-changing environment. We continuously innovate and drive constructive change while keeping a focus on the “big picture.” We exercise sound business judgment in making high-quality decisions in a timely and cost-effective manner. We are highly creative and can dig deep within ourselves to find positive solutions to different problems.

Juice - The “Stuff” it takes to be a Needle Mover

We get things done and drive results. We lead without a title, empowering others through a can-do attitude. We look forward to the goal, mentally mapping out every checkpoint on the pathway to success, and visualizing what the final destination looks and feels like.

Teamwork - Humble, Hungry and Smart

We are humble individuals who understand how our job impacts the company's mission. We treat others with respect, admit mistakes, give credit where it’s due and demonstrate transparency. We “bring the weather” by exhibiting positive leadership and solution-focused thinking. We hug people in their trials, struggles, and failures – not just their success. We appreciate the individuality of the people around us.

JOB SUMMARY:

In this role, you will own advanced analytics and modeling for Trace3 Revenue Operations. This is a senior individual contributor position, and you will focus on three questions the business cannot answer with confidence today: what actually drives win and loss, what an opportunity’s propensity to close is at each stage, and which offering a given client is most likely to purchase next.

You will build AI-enabled models across market, client, and sales activity data against outcomes, and you will own the measurement system the sales organization is managed by — including a leading-indicator index of sales play activity and the correlation testing that must pass before anyone is asked to manage to it.

Your first deliverable is an honest assessment of what is inferable from the data we have and a specification of what the data foundation must fix for everything else. In this role you are a forcing function on data quality, not a consumer waiting on it.

SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

Win/Loss and Propensity Modeling

• You will build and validate models identifying the drivers of win and loss across segments, offerings, and partner motions.

• You’ll model propensity to close by opportunity stage, and quantify the confidence and the limits of each model.

• You will build targeting models that predict propensity to purchase one offering versus another at the account level.

• You’ll translate model output into specific, testable recommendations and get them into the sellers’ workflow rather than into a slide.

Leading-Indicator Measurement

• You will own the design of a weighted index of sales play activity — plays initiated, stage progression, certified sellers active in a play, partner co-sell motions run — setting activity definitions and weights alongside regional and vertical sales leaders.

• You’ll test the correlation between that index and bookings one to two quarters forward, and publish the result, before the index is used as a management tool.

• You will own the Revenue Operations scoreboard: measure definitions, calculations, baselines, and automated weekly delivery.

Advanced Analytics and Reporting

• You will deliver AI-native analytics and reporting faster than traditional BI development cycles allow.

• You’ll establish the renewal capture rate baseline and the installed-base renewals measurement that services margin performance depends on.

• You will build reporting leaders act on, and retire reporting nobody uses.

• You’ll report findings to senior leadership, including where the data does not support a conclusion.

Data Foundation Advocacy

• You will specify what customer master data, account parenting, and required-field completeness must reach for each modeling use case, and hold the data governance work to those requirements.

• You’ll define and maintain a composite data quality measure covering duplicate account rate, parenting coverage, and field completeness.

• You will partner with our AI Engineer, who builds the delivery mechanism, while you build the inference underneath it.

Cross-Functional Partnership

• You will partner with regional and segment sales leadership, Finance, Marketing, IT, and the Transformation Office.

• You’ll defend a method to a sales leader who does not trust the answer — and change the method when the objection is right.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

The right candidate for this role will bring:

• A bachelor’s degree in statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, operations research, or a related quantitative field; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.

• 7+ years in data science, decision science, or advanced analytics, with a record of models that changed a business decision.

• Demonstrated experience modeling commercial outcomes: win/loss, propensity to close, churn, next-best-action, or account and territory targeting.

• Strong applied statistics — experimental design, causal inference, survival analysis — and the judgment to know which applies.

• Fluency in Python or R and in SQL, with experience in modern ML tooling and LLM-assisted analysis workflows.

• Experience building analytics on CRM, ERP, and sales activity data, including the data quality problems that come with it.

• The ability to work productively with imperfect data and to state plainly what cannot yet be concluded.

• Experience defining and defending a measurement framework to senior commercial leaders.

• A bias toward AI-enabled modeling and automation over hand-built recurring reporting.

• A senior individual contributor orientation. This role has no direct reports and you will influence through the quality of your work.

• Experience in technology services, consulting, or a systems integrator environment preferred.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain a method to a non-technical audience without diluting it.

Actual salary will be based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, skill set, performance, licensure and certification, and business needs. The range for this position in other geographic locations may differ. Certain positions may also be eligible for variable incentive compensation, such as bonuses or commissions, that is not included in the base salary.
Estimated Pay Range
$150,000—$200,000 USD

The Perks

  • Comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans for you and your dependents
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match, 529 College Savings Plan, Health Savings Account, Life Insurance, and Long-Term Disability
  • Competitive Compensation
  • Training and development programs
  • Major offices stocked with snacks and beverages
  • Collaborative and cool culture
  • Work-life balance and generous paid time off

Our Commitment

At the core of Trace3's DNA is our people. We are a diverse group of talented individuals who understand the importance of teamwork and demonstrating leadership, character, and passion in all that we do.

We’re committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to grow. We recognize that embracing diversity drives innovation, improves outcomes, fosters collaboration, boosts teammate satisfaction, and builds a more inclusive culture.

As an equal opportunity employer, Trace3 bases all employment decisions based on individual qualifications, merit, and business requirements. We do not engage in discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), national origin, age (40 or older), disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Any demographic information provided is strictly voluntary, kept confidential in accordance with Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) regulations, and will not be used in employment decisions, including hiring, promotions, or mentorship programs. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all.

About Flexspring

Flexspring is the leading expert in data integration for HR applications. We work with various clients to build customized integrations that will solve their specific HR business needs.

The Opportunity

The IT Operations role is to oversee the configuration, deployment, and daily operation of the internal IT systems and hardware used by the company’s employees. While the Cloud Engineering team manages the infrastructure for our cloud-based solution, the IT Ops Specialist is responsible for the internal corporate environment. This role focuses on providing exceptional technical support, managing corporate devices (including provisioning), and ensuring a secure, efficient IT experience for all employees from their first day to their last.

Your Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the IT onboarding and offboarding processes, including account creation, license allocation, and access configuration. Ensure secure access revocation and hardware recovery upon employee departures.
  • Configure, deploy, and maintain corporate laptops (Windows, Linux, and Mac), peripherals, and mobile devices to ensure employees have the tools they need to succeed.
  • Administer Google Workspace and support Google Workspace users
  • Administer Office 365 and support users (Teams, Outlook, etc)
  • Maintain a rigorous and accurate inventory of all corporate IT assets and hardware lifecycle.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for employee technical requests (Helpdesk) using Jira Service Management (JSM). Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, and corporate network issues promptly and courteously.
  • Administer JumpCloud for identity, access, and device management across both PC and Mac fleets to automate device setup, policies, and OS updates.
  • Enforce corporate endpoint security policies and conduct continuous auditing of all laptops using Elastic Security and Elastic Fleet, ensuring workstations remain compliant with company IT security standards.
  • Create and maintain internal user guides and IT Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) within Confluence to promote employee autonomy and team knowledge sharing.
  • Assist in managing on-site IT infrastructure, such as office networking (Wi-Fi, VPN access) and conference room A/V equipment
  • Assist the Cloud Ops team with various tasks when available and necessary.

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary
  • Work with cutting-edge technology in the growing field of data integration.
  • Own your success: Receive an attractive base salary, enjoy an empowering work culture, and apply your expertise to meaningful work.

  • 2-3 years of experience in a technical support, helpdesk, or corporate IT operations role.

  • Understanding of basic corporate networking concepts (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, Wi-Fi).
  • Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure services (AWS or equivalent) and database management systems (RDS, MongoDB, Redis, Elastic etc).
  • Solid understanding of core IT security principles, including the CIA triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability).

  • Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and customer service skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to non-technical users.
  • Strong interest for AI tools and how they can be used to improve the effectiveness of the organization’s services

Nice to Have

  • Knowledge of ITIL best practices for IT Service Management.
  • Familiarity with automation scripting (e.g., PowerShell, Bash, Python) for automating routine internal IT tasks.
  • Relevant IT certifications (e.g., CompTIA A+, Network+, or OS-specific certifications).
  • Familiarity with container-based services (Docker, Kubernetes, Swarm Manager)

  • Experience with endpoint security monitoring and auditing tools (knowledge of Elastic Security and Elastic Fleet is highly advantageous).
  • Professional or Native French.

jobs.title: Compliance Officer
jobs.excerpt: WHO IS RATEHUB?  We’re a company on a mission.  We are a unique Canadian Fintech that is the one-stop shop for all financial needs of the consumer: Save, Spend, Borrow, Invest, and Protect.
jobs.description:
WHO IS RATEHUB?

We’re a company on a mission. We are a unique Canadian Fintech that is the one-stop shop for all financial needs of the consumer: Save, Spend, Borrow, Invest, and Protect. Every single team member — from Product & Engineering to Sales & Marketing, Finance, Operations, and everything in between — is obsessed with one thing: helping Canadians make better financial choices. And we’re pretty great at it, too. Via our digital application technology and our award-winning in-house brokerages, we help over 2M Canadians per month make a positive impact on their finances. We have many unique businesses: a mortgage brokerage, a life insurance brokerage, a home and auto insurance brokerage, a mortgage originations and servicing business, a Financial Services Marketplace, and a content business across Ratehub and MoneySense. 365 days a year, we deliver our users the best online mortgage experience, personalized credit card and loan options, and cheaper auto and home insurance policies than they typically get from their existing financial adviser.

Changing how people make financial choices isn’t easy, though. We know that achieving our mission is full of challenges — challenges that can be complex and often unexpected but that are always interesting, rewarding, and fun to solve as a team. This is where you come in. We are on the hunt for the right candidate to join us and help lead us forward to continued growth.

About the role

The Compliance Officer is the accountable owner of the company's compliance programs across every regulated entity: the mortgage brokerage, the CMHC-approved mortgage lender, and the P&C and life insurance brokerages. They report to the VP of Finance & Operations.

Roles and responsibilities

Program ownership and governance

  • Maintain the existing compliance framework across all entities, including the register of regulatory obligations mapped to owners and controls, and update it as rules and the business change.
  • Serve as the designated AML compliance officer for the company's FINTRAC reporting entities and as the company's privacy officer.
  • Own licence renewal tracking and agent onboarding checks with expanding support of the sales team leaders as capacity allows.
  • Report compliance status, issues and remediation progress to Sr. Management
  • Monitor regulatory change across provincial and federal regimes and assess its impact on the business.

Licensing and registrations

  • Maintain entity, brokerage, broker/agent and insurance licences and registrations in every province where the company operates.
  • Manage renewals, new-province applications, agent onboarding and offboarding checks, continuing-education tracking and E&O coverage requirements.

Regulatory reporting and examinations

  • Own the calendar of regulatory filings and deliver annual filings to provincial regulators, CMHC approved-lender requirements and FINTRAC reports on time.
  • Lead regulator examinations and audits, coordinate responses and track remediation to closure.

Complaints and market conduct (oversight)

  • Own the complaint-handling policy and complaints register; review escalations, report trends and meet regulator and ombudsman reporting requirements.
  • Run periodic file reviews and testing of disclosure, suitability, conflicts of interest and fair treatment of customers.

AML/FINTRAC and privacy

  • Own the AML program: keep policies, the risk assessment, client identification and record-keeping procedures and training current, and coordinate the two-year effectiveness review.
  • Own the privacy program under PIPEDA, Quebec's Law 25 and CASL, keeping consent, partner data-sharing and breach-response procedures current.

Policies and procedures

  • Maintain the compliance manual and policy library, run the annual policy review and collect staff attestations.

Key qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years of compliance experience in Canadian regulated financial services, in either mortgage brokerage/lending or insurance brokerage, and the ability to learn the other quickly.
  • Working knowledge of provincial regulatory regimes (e.g., FSRA, BCFSA, AMF), FINTRAC/PCMLTFA obligations and PIPEDA.
  • Hands-on experience running licensing, regulatory filings and regulator examinations.
  • Experience reviewing and updating established compliance policies and programs.
  • Strong writing skills for policies, procedures and regulator correspondence.
  • Highly organized and deadline-driven, with a track record of managing many renewal and filing dates at once.
  • Ability to influence sales and operations leaders without direct authority.

Preferred

  • A compliance or privacy designation such as CAMS or CIPP/C.
  • A current or past mortgage or insurance licence.
  • Experience managing compliance across multiple regulated entities or provinces.
  • Bilingual in English and French.
  • Interest in growing into people leadership.

CULTURE FIT:

Members first - we prioritise the interests and needs of our members above all else.We solve member pain points and focus on member satisfaction. We start with members, and end with the P&L.
Growth mindset - we set ambitious goals and challenge the status quo. We take responsible risks and are accountable for our actions.
Better together - we are One team with One common goal. We make our footprint bigger than our foot, leave our egos at the door, support each other to achieve great results as One company.
Run after problems - we tackle problems head on and focus on finding solutions. Obstacles are seen as opportunities for growth and innovation. We have the hard conversations and choose the harder right over the easier wrong. And we do it with a smile
Measure Learn Iterate Innovate - we focus on getting things done. We measure what matters, iterate, learn, iterate many times in a data-driven way, which is how we will innovate.

JOB PERKS:

Competitive Compensation: A salary that reflects your experience and the Canadian market.
Remote-First Environment: The flexibility to work from anywhere in Canada, with occasional in-person team gatherings for collaboration.
Flexible Hours: Autonomy to manage your schedule to support work-life balance.
Professional Development: An individual training allowance to help you grow your skills and career.
Team Socials: Regular events, both remote and in-person, to build connections across the organization.

The estimated salary range for this position is $95,000 - $130,000.

This job posting is for a currently open vacancy.

About Leo Berwick

Leo Berwick is a boutique tax and deal advisory firm built around infrastructure and energy transition. We are not generalists who happen to cover the sector - it is the whole of what we do, and it is why sponsors, developers, and funds bring us their most technical transactions.

Leo Berwick UK is an independent, partner-led practice, established as a UK LLP and run from London by its own founding Partnership team and Management Committee. Where a mandate is genuinely cross-border, we draw on the wider Leo Berwick network across North America and Europe.

You’ll have the autonomy of a partner-led firm with direct access to its Partners. Your contribution will be visible, your ideas will have an impact, and you’ll be recognized for what you help build as the practice grows.

What we’re looking for

We’re looking for a Vice President, Deal Advisory to join our founding London team. This is a build role, not just a seat. You’ll work directly with Partners on live transactions while playing a central role in shaping how the practice uses AI, automation and proprietary tools to deliver faster, sharper and more efficient advice.

You’re the right fit for this role if –

  • You’re at a Big 4 or leading advisory firm and want more ownership, pace and recognition than a large organisation allows.

  • You’re as comfortable building a tool or automating a workflow as you are running a deal.
  • You thrive in an entrepreneurial environment and want to be rewarded for the value you create.

What you'll do

  • Deal execution: Lead diligence and structuring workstreams on small, mid and large-cap private equity transactions, from scoping through to completion.

  • AI and automation: Lead the practice’s adoption of AI and process automation to reduce manual effort, accelerate turnaround times and raise the quality of delivery.
  • Tool development: Partner with technology teams to design, build and deploy diligence and tax tools that automate core deal processes.
  • Practice building: Help shape the practice’s delivery model, methodologies and templates; support Partners on proposals and business development; and mentor Senior Associates.

What you bring

  • 5+ years’ experience in transaction services, financial due diligence or a related deal advisory role.
  • ACA, ACCA or equivalent chartered accountancy qualification, ideally with first-time passes.
  • Hands-on experience running funds flows and deal execution for PE clients across small, mid and large-cap transactions.
  • Advanced Excel skills, with experience building and reviewing complex models.
  • Strong AI proficiency, with hands-on experience using VBA and other process automation tools.
  • Experience working with technology or product teams to turn deal processes into scalable tools.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, and the ability to perform under deal pressure.
  • Exposure to infrastructure and energy transition transactions is welcome but not essential.

  • Flexible working arrangements – remote and location flexibility
  • Study and professional subscription support
  • Childcare support
  • Private medical and dental cover
  • Pension contributions
  • Monthly well-being allowance
  • Further benefits to support your physical and mental wellbeing

This job description does not constitute an employment agreement and is subject to change as the needs of Cotiviti and requirements of the job change.

  • Technical Aptitude: You don’t need to code, but you must be technically fluent. You can hold your ground with a program’s Chief Architect or a DevSecOps lead about Kubernetes, software factories, and air-gapped or classified environments.

  • Methodology Master: You live and breathe sales methodology. You can clearly explain how you use MEDDPICC/MEDDIC to qualify federal deals and de-risk a pipeline that depends on funding and contract timing.

  • Consistency: A documented history of performing in the top 10 to 20% of your cohort. We want to see President’s Club awards and consistent quota over-achievement.

  • Start-Up Grit: Experience in a high-growth environment. You are comfortable with ambiguity and willing to build the federal playbook, not just read it.

Bonus points for:

  • Partner Ecosystem: Established relationships with major federal systems integrators and resellers, and experience co-selling through them.

  • Startup Experience: You have been at an early-stage organization where you control your own desk, operate autonomously, and build something from zero.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

Standard Job Description

Shape the future of AI at Lockheed Martin and help advance responsible AI beyond our enterprise. We are seeking an AI Research Engineer Stf (Level 4) to serve as an AI Vantage Research Lead. AI Vantage is a new internal think tank in the AI Certifications & Standards (AI-CS) directorate within the Lockheed Martin Artificial Intelligence Center (LAIC). You will combine hands-on technical research with business insight to anticipate enterprise-wide AI risks and influence how Lockheed Martin develops and applies the next generation of AI capabilities.

AI Vantage's mandate is to "See farther. Decide better." You will investigate alignment, safety, increasing autonomy, and risks that span portfolios and long horizons, challenge assumptions, and turn findings into strategies that accelerate responsible AI adoption. Your work will inform enterprise decisions with lasting implications for AI strategy and governance, and contribute to responsible AI thought leadership beyond Lockheed Martin. You will advance our AI Governance mission: "Accelerating AI. Earning trust."

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with substantial independence. Initially, leadership responsibilities will focus on guiding specific research efforts, coordinating contributors, and sharing technical expertise. As AI Vantage scales, your technical and project leadership responsibilities will grow to encompass broader research initiatives.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with the AI Vantage Manager to develop and maintain a long-term roadmap for managing enterprise AI risk, connecting research priorities with business and mission objectives.
  • Design and conduct hands-on technical research on emerging AI capabilities, including alignment, safety, and increasing autonomy, to assess their implications for Lockheed Martin.
  • Test enterprise AI risk hypotheses using business and technical analysis, informed by research literature and stakeholder insights. Use model evaluations, prototypes, or other investigative tools as appropriate to answer specific research questions.
  • Contribute new concepts, research methods, and innovative solutions to complex enterprise AI risk problems, applying expertise in AI and related disciplines and a thorough understanding of industry and company practices.
  • Define and execute research approaches without day-to-day direction. Completed work is reviewed for technical quality and consistency with departmental objectives.
  • Conduct cross-portfolio risk studies to identify shared dependencies, vulnerabilities, and compounding risks across business areas and enterprise functions.
  • Develop long-horizon AI risk scenarios, identify early warning indicators, and recommend actions the enterprise should consider now.
  • Develop AI incident scenarios with business areas and enterprise functions to inform preparedness, accountability, and response decisions.
  • Translate research into written analyses and briefings for senior business and technical personnel on significant AI risks. Explain evidence, uncertainty, options, and recommendations that influence long-term enterprise strategy and AI governance.
  • Collaborate with AI Red Teaming and Standards & Partnerships on risk investigations and incorporate their findings into enterprise analysis. Partner with AI Rigor to inform AI governance evolution.
  • Help shape AI Vantage's research priorities and guide major research projects to completion, defining milestones and deliverables and maintaining visibility into progress and commitments.
  • Collaborate with enterprise functions to develop mitigation plans for identified enterprise AI risks, agree on accountable owners and milestones, and track actions through completion.

Basic Qualifications

  • Demonstrated technical expertise in AI, machine learning, data science, or analytics, with a thorough understanding of relevant industry practices and related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently on complex, ambiguous problems, develop innovative approaches, and synthesize incomplete or conflicting evidence into defensible conclusions.
  • Experience translating technical findings into recommendations that support business, mission, or enterprise decisions.
  • Experience guiding technical projects or research efforts to completion and collaborating with business and technical contributors in a distributed environment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex findings, assumptions, uncertainty, and recommendations to senior business and technical personnel.
  • Prior experience using an agile framework, such as Scrum, SAFe, or Kanban, to plan and deliver research or technical project work.

Desired Skills

  • Prior public policy experience related to AI, data, or analytics, such as policy analysis, policy development, or work with government and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Prior business strategy experience in AI, data, or analytics, including developing enterprise strategies, adoption roadmaps, investment priorities, or business cases tied to mission and business value.
  • Experience with strategic foresight, horizon scanning, scenario planning, or research on risks that span organizations or portfolios.
  • Experience producing executive-level research, thought leadership, or decision support that influences strategy or governance.
  • Prior experience in one or more Lockheed Martin business areas, including Aeronautics, Missiles & Fire Control, Rotary & Mission Systems, or Space.
  • Prior experience within Lockheed Martin Enterprise Operations with a demonstrated ability to build cross-organizational partnerships that achieve mutual objectives.
  • Prior experience with a major consulting firm, advising clients on enterprise strategy, organizational transformation, or complex business and technology challenges.
  • Experience improving cross-disciplinary collaboration, challenging assumptions, and influencing outcomes without formal authority.
  • Experience researching risks associated with advanced AI models, agentic AI, or autonomous capabilities, including reliability, human oversight, or potential failure modes.
  • Experience applying state-of-the-art (SOTA) AI models to deliver demonstrated business value.

THE COMPANY

DTiQ is a global leader in intelligent video-based surveillance and loss prevention solutions, helping businesses improve operations and protect their assets.
